purpose: Test mechanisms before inspecting their numerical gradient results; frozen checkpoint copies only

hypotheses.mechanism: L(delta)=sign(delta)*exp(-abs(delta)) is discontinuous at zero. Away from zero its ordinary derivative is -exp(-abs(delta)), but a finite crossing adds an approximately 2-unit jump. Autodiff is correct within a branch and does not predict crossings.
hypotheses.prediction: Finite loss changes along a descent direction depart from its gradient prediction when crossings appear; holding baseline branch masks fixed reduces this discrepancy.
hypotheses.test: FP64 finite differences and phase-only update interventions; control uses the identical forward at the unperturbed point and a replayed sign mask at every block.

hypotheses.mechanism: h -> mean(h+injection) -> RMSNorm -> W_phase -> phase/window -> attention -> next h creates a feedback derivative in addition to the activity path.
hypotheses.prediction: Detaching only the summary leaves outputs/loss unchanged but materially changes recurrent state gradients and contributions to shared phase parameters.
hypotheses.test: Unroll 8 blocks with identical forward, compare full gradient against summary-detached gradient; quantify gradient norm and temporal cancellation.

hypotheses.mechanism: Changes of the pooled state, amplified by summary normalization and aligned phase projections, move many channel-pair delays across zero.
hypotheses.prediction: At frozen weights signs keep switching; state/summary lag correlations, projection gains and attention/FFN decomposition identify oscillation or irregular dynamics. Lower phase gain or freezing the summary can reduce hidden-state changes.
hypotheses.test: Frozen-weight 16-block traces and isolated phase-gain, frozen-summary, attention and FFN interventions on the same saved puzzles.

controls: Same raw weights, inputs, initial carry and data labels within comparisons
Direct probe vs production FP32 block parity before gradient experiments
FP64 algebraic replica for finite differences to avoid BF16/FP32 quantization
Observations on small frozen subsets are not proof of improved retraining performance
live_training: No stop, parameter update or configuration change to the running experiment
